step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows FINRA's analytics data lake and data mart generation solution on AWS. 1. Data management ETL processes copy gold source data into an S3 Data Lake. 2. A user submits an analytical query to an ECS service. 3. ECS kicks off a Hive job on an EMR cluster (step 1) which reads data from the S3 Data Lake and writes a subset materialized Data Mart back into S3. 4. ECS inspects the Data Mart for query complexity (step 2) and routes the request based on complexity: simple queries go to Presto on EMR, while complex multi-dataset join queries are routed to Redshift. 5. Both Presto EMR and Redshift pull the materialized data directly from the S3 Data Mart to perform interactive queries.

graph.name: FINRA Analytics Data Lake Architecture
graph.notes: FINRA processes up to 135 billion daily market events using AWS analytics tools, dynamically selecting Presto EMR or Redshift based on query complexity.

nodes.notes: Data management and ETL processing pipeline.

nodes.name: S3 Data Lake
nodes.notes: Multi-petabyte S3 bucket holding analytics copy of gold source data.

nodes.name: HIVE EMR
nodes.notes: EMR cluster running Hive to pair down lake data into data marts.

nodes.name: S3 Data Mart
nodes.notes: S3 bucket storing materialized data mart subsets for analytical querying.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: ECS container service orchestrating query processing, data mart jobs, and engine selection.

nodes.name: PRESTO EMR
nodes.notes: EMR cluster running Presto engine for interactive, low-complexity queries.

nodes.name: REDSHIFT
nodes.notes: Redshift cluster used for high-complexity, large row-count queries with multi-dataset joins.
